record.title: Diagonal Ramsey bound for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph on $n$ vertices, and let $R(H,H)$ denote its diagonal two-colour Ramsey number. **The planar Ramsey conjecture.** For every sufficiently large $n$ and every planar graph $H$ on $n$ vertices, 
$$
R(H,H)\leq 12n.
$$
 The source explains that a linear bound is known for all planar graphs and that the constant $12$ is known for bounded-degree planar graphs; the conjecture proposes the same constant without the bounded-degree assumption.
record.source_name: Peter Allen, Graham Brightwell and Jozef Skokan, “Ramsey-goodness – and otherwise”, arXiv:1010.5079 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5079

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

record.title: Chetwynd–Hilton 1-factorization conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a regular simple graph of order $2n$, with degree at least $n$. A **1-factorization** of $G$ is a decomposition of its edge set into perfect matchings.

**Chetwynd–Hilton 1-factorization conjecture.** Every regular simple graph of order $2n$ and degree at least $n$ is 1-factorizable.

This conjecture, formulated by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1985, is the classical 1-Factorization Conjecture. If true, it would imply that for every regular graph of even order, at least one of the graph and its complement is 1-factorizable.
record.source_name: E. R. Vaughan, “An Asymptotic Version of the Multigraph 1-Factorization Conjecture”, arXiv:1010.5192 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5192

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

record.title: Stronger transcendence conclusion for equal exponential powers
record.statement:
Let $r,s,t$ be as in the preceding proposition: $r,s,t$ are positive real numbers with $s<t$ and $s^{\,t}=t^{\,s}=r$, where $r>e^{\,e}$. Under either of the following conditions, at least one of $s$ and $t$ is known to be transcendental: (i) $16\neq r\in\mathbb{N}$, or (ii) $r^n\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

**Stronger transcendence conclusion.** Under the hypotheses of Proposition $(i)RT=TR=A$, both $s$ and $t$ are transcendental.

This prediction strengthens the proposition's unconditional conclusion from at least one transcendental number to both numbers being transcendental. The source attributes it to an earlier conjecture and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Diego Marques and Jonathan Sondow, “Schanuel's conjecture and algebraic powers z^w and w^z with z and w transcendental”, arXiv:1010.6216 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.6216

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2010). “In particular, $\pi + e$ and $\pi e$ are transcendental. (These conclusions are all open problems if $(S)$ is not assumed.”

record.title: Fang–Zhang–Zhang conjecture for normalized Ricci flow
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a closed oriented smooth Riemannian $4$-manifold. Write $\lVert X\rVert$ for its Gromov simplicial volume and $\bar{\lambda}(X)$ for Perelman's invariant. A solution to the normalized Ricci flow on $X$ is **quasi-non-singular** if it exists for all time and has uniformly bounded scalar curvature. Assume that

$$
\lVert X\rVert \ne 0,\qquad \bar{\lambda}(X)<0,
$$

and that $X$ admits a quasi-non-singular solution. **Fang–Zhang–Zhang conjecture.** Then

$$
2e(X)-3|\operatorname{sign}(X)|\geq \frac{1}{1295\pi^2}\lVert X\rVert.
$$

This conjecture predicts a Gromov–Hitchin–Thorpe type topological inequality for four-manifolds supporting such Ricci-flow solutions. The source states that it remains open; the stronger Einstein-case inequality discussed there motivates it.
record.source_name: R. Inanc Baykur and Masashi Ishida, “Families of 4-manifolds with nontrivial stable cohomotopy Seiberg-Witten invariants, and normalized Ricci flow”, arXiv:1011.2744 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.2744

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2010). “To the best of our knowledge, the FZZ conjecture remains open.”

record.title: The completeness conjecture for Constructions A, B and C
record.statement: Let $PG(2,q)$ be the projective plane of order $q$. Constructions A, B, and C produce families of complete $k$-arcs in the size regions stated in the paper's theorem: Construction A for prime $q$, Construction B for prime powers $q\not\equiv3\pmod 4$, and Construction C for prime powers $q\equiv3\pmod4$, with the corresponding bounds on $k$ and the listed verified exceptional ranges. **Completeness conjecture for Constructions A, B and C.** The assertions of that theorem hold also for every $q>1367$. This would extend the experimentally verified completeness of the three construction families beyond the ranges proved in the paper.
record.source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Alexander A. Davydov, Giorgio Faina, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “On sizes of complete arcs in PG(2,q)”, arXiv:1011.3347 (2011).

record.title: Caporossi–Cvetković–Gutman–Hansen conjecture on maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices. Let $P_n^6$ be the unicyclic graph obtained by connecting a vertex of the cycle $C_6$ to a leaf of the path $P_{n-6}$. For a graph $G$ with adjacency-matrix eigenvalues $lambda_1,ldots,lambda_n$, its **energy** is

$$
E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n|\lambda_i|.
$$

**Caporossi–Cvetković–Gutman–Hansen conjecture.** Among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, the cycle $C_n$ has maximal energy if $n\leq 7$ or $n\in\{9,10,11,13,15\}$. For all other values of $n$, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is $P_n^6$.

The conjecture identifies the extremal unicyclic graph by the number of vertices and concerns the adjacency-spectrum energy of graphs. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Bofeng Huo, Xueliang Li and Yongtang Shi, “Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:1011.4658 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

record.title: Rational-Weierstrass genus-2 Jacobian prime-order conjecture
record.statement:
For a prime $p>2$, let $P_1(p)$ be the probability that a uniformly randomly chosen integer in the Hasse–Weil interval $[(\sqrt p-1)^4,(\sqrt p+1)^4]$ is prime, and let $P_2(p)$ be the probability that a genus-$2$ curve with a rational Weierstrass point, obtained by choosing $f$ uniformly from the monic square-free degree-$5$ polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$, has a Jacobian with a prime number of rational points. Let $c_p$ be the constant in the genus-$2$ Jacobian prime-order conjecture. **Rational-Weierstrass prime-order conjecture.** Then

$$
\lim_{p\to\infty}\left(P_2(p)/P_1(p)-\frac{9}{19}c_p\right)=0.
$$

The factor $9/19$ reflects the increased probability of rational $2$-torsion, making prime orders substantially less likely; the claim is heuristic and remains unproved.
record.source_name: Wouter Castryck, Amanda Folsom, Hendrik Hubrechts and Andrew V. Sutherland, “The probability that the number of points on the Jacobian of a genus 2 curve is prime”, arXiv:1101.4792 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4792

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: Higher Noether--Lefschetz gaps for the four categorical examples
record.statement:
Consider the Artin--Mumford example, $V_{10}$ with $10$ singular points, the double covering of a quadric ramified in an octic with $20$ nodal singular points, and the double solid ramified in a sextic with $35$ singular points. Let $NLGap(D^b(X))$ denote the maximal gap in the enhanced Noether--Lefschetz spectrum. **Higher Noether--Lefschetz gap conjecture.** For all four examples,

$$
NLGap(D^b(X))\geq 2.
$$

Together with the predicted ordinary gap equal to one, this would distinguish the enhanced spectrum from the ordinary Orlov spectrum, but the statement is explicitly conjectural in the source.
record.source_name: Atanas Iliev, Ludmil Katzarkov and Victor Przyjalkowski, “Double solids, categories and non-rationality”, arXiv:1102.2130 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.2130

record.title: Vanishing of the cotangent cohomology for flag combinatorial spheres
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a combinatorial sphere and a flag complex. For every codimension-$2$ face $f$, let $\operatorname{lk}(f,\mathcal{K})$ denote its link, and let $A_{\mathcal{K}}$ be the Stanley–Reisner ring of $\mathcal{K}$. 

**Vanishing conjecture.** If $\operatorname{lk}(f,\mathcal{K})$ is a $4$-gon or a $5$-gon for every codimension-$2$ face $f$, then

$$
T^2_{A_{\mathcal{K}}}=0.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations for flag $3$-spheres obtained by successive edge starrings, as well as by the corresponding result in dimension $2$. The stated computations found trivial $T^2$ in all $74$ examples considered, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Jan Arthur Christophersen and Nathan Owen Ilten, “Degenerations to Unobstructed Fano Stanley-Reisner Schemes”, arXiv:1102.4521 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.4521

record.title: 576-periodicity conjecture for free fermion conformal nets
record.statement:
Let $\mathit{Fer}(n)$ denote the conformal net of $n$ free fermions, and let $\mathit{CN}$ denote the 3-category of conformal nets, with its notion of $\mathit{CN}$-equivalence. For every integer $n$, **the 576-periodicity conjecture** asserts that there exists a $\mathit{CN}$-equivalence between

$$
\mathit{Fer}(n)\quad\text{and}\quad\mathit{Fer}(n+576).
$$

The conjecture proposes a conformal-net analogue of the 8-fold Morita periodicity of real Clifford algebras and of the 576-periodicity of topological modular forms. The corresponding algebraic periodicity for free fermion nets had not been established in the source.
record.source_name: Christopher L. Douglas and André G. Henriques, “Topological modular forms and conformal nets”, arXiv:1103.4187 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4187

record.title: The weak DRY conjecture for stable bundles on Calabi–Yau threefolds
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Calabi–Yau threefold with $pi_1(X)=0$. For $c\in H^4(X,\mathbf{Z})$, call $c$ a **DRY class** if there exist an ample class $H\in H^2(X,\mathbf{R})$ and an integer $\mathcal{N}$ such that

$$
c=\mathcal{N}\left(H^2+\frac{c_2(X)}{24}\right).
$$

Call $c$ a **Chern class** if there exists a stable $SU(\mathcal{N})$ vector bundle $V$ on $X$ with $c=c_2(V)$. **Weak DRY conjecture.** Every DRY class $c\in H^4(X,\mathbf{Z})$ is a Chern class.

The conjecture gives a sufficient condition for a cohomology class to occur as the second Chern class of a stable vector bundle with trivial first Chern class. The paper proves it for all ranks $\mathcal{N}\geq 4$ in the stated elliptically fibered cases, apart from finitely many exceptions, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Bjorn Andreas and Gottfried Curio, “On the Existence of Stable bundles with prescribed Chern classes on Calabi-Yau threefolds”, arXiv:1104.3435 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3435

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

record.title: The three-distinct-odd-prime refinement of the weak Goldbach conjecture
record.statement:
Let $Prime(q)$ be the quota complex formed from odd primes whose total sum is below $q$, and let $H_2(Prime(q),\mathbb{Q})$ denote its second homology group. **The three-distinct-odd-prime Goldbach conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{dim}(H_2(Prime(q),\mathbb{Q})) \neq 0
$$

for all $q\geq 20$. Equivalently, every odd number $q\geq 19$ is a sum of exactly three distinct odd primes.

The paper describes this as a refinement of the weak Goldbach conjecture and bases it on data through $q=550$. It notes that the weak Goldbach conjecture was known there for almost all odd numbers, but does not give a resolution of this distinct-prime refinement.
record.source_name: Jonathan Pakianathan and Troy Winfree, “Quota Complexes, Persistant Homology and the Goldbach Conjecture”, arXiv:1104.4324 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.4324

record.title: Kenyon–Smillie conjecture on lattice-property rational triangles
record.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, and $t$ be integers with $(n,s)=1$ and $1\leq s,t<n$. Assume that for every integer $p$ with $(p,n)=1$,

$$
\frac{n}{2}<ps\bmod n+pt\bmod n<\frac{3n}{2}.
$$

**Kenyon–Smillie conjecture.** One of the following conditions holds: $n\leq 78$, $s+t=n$, $s+2t=n$, $2s+t=n$, or $n$ is even and $|t-s|=\frac{n}{2}$. This arithmetic conjecture would remove the denominator bound in Kenyon and Smillie's classification of acute non-isosceles rational-angled triangles with the lattice property.
record.source_name: Jan-Christoph Schlage-Puchta, “On triangular billiards”, arXiv:1105.1629 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1629

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

record.title: The length-five even-Wilf-equivalence conjectures
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}_n(sigma)$ denote the set of even permutations in $\mathcal{S}_n$ avoiding the pattern $sigma$, and write $sigma equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} tau$ when these avoidance sets have the same cardinality for every $n$. The patterns below are conjectured to be even-Wilf-equivalent:

**Even-Wilf-equivalence conjecture.**

$$
12345 equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} 45312,
$$

$$
54321 equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} 21354,
$$

$$
12354 equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} 45321,
$$

$$
13524 equiv_{\mathcal{E}_n} 42531.
$$

These equivalences are conjectured from numerical data through $n\folio 11$; the first and second are related by a symmetry.
record.source_name: Andrew M. Baxter and Aaron D. Jaggard, “Pattern avoidance by even permutations”, arXiv:1106.3653 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3653

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2011).

record.title: The Stankova–West even-shape-Wilf-equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
For a permutation pattern $sigma$ and a Ferrers shape $lambda$, let $E_{lambda}(sigma)$ be the even transversals of $lambda$ that avoid $sigma$. Two patterns are **even-shape-Wilf-equivalent** when these sets have equal cardinality for every Ferrers shape. The conjecture is:

**Stankova–West conjecture.**

$$
312 text{ is even-shape-Wilf-equivalent to }231.
$$

This is the even analogue of the Stankova–West equivalence and, if true, would complete the classification of patterns of length six; the paper reports computational verification in bounded Ferrers shapes.
record.source_name: Andrew M. Baxter and Aaron D. Jaggard, “Pattern avoidance by even permutations”, arXiv:1106.3653 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3653

record.title: The strict inequality between dismal divisor counts and their sum
record.statement:
Let $d_{10}(n)$ denote the number of dismal divisors of $n$ in base $10$, and let $\sigma_{10}(n)$ denote the dismal sum of those divisors. **Dismal divisor-sum inequality.** For every integer $n>1$,

$$
d_{10}(n)<\sigma_{10}(n).
$$

The conjecture compares the number of dismal divisors with their dismal sum. It is presented as an unresolved conjecture at the end of the section, with no proof or resolution given.
record.source_name: David Applegate, Marc LeBrun and N. J. A. Sloane, “Dismal Arithmetic”, arXiv:1107.1130 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

record.title: The integrality conjecture for the coefficients in the L-polynomials
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive even integer and let $\sigma$ be a pairing of $\{1,\dots,n\}$. Theorem stated in the source says that $Z_\sigma/Z_{1|2|\cdots|n}$ is a polynomial of degree $n/2$ in the quantities

$$
\{L_{i,j}:1\leq i<j\leq n\}\quad\text{and}\quad\{L'_{i,j}:1\leq i<j\leq n-1\}.
$$

**Integrality conjecture.** Every coefficient of these polynomials is an integer.

The claim was verified in the source for all pairings $\sigma$ and all $n\leq 10$, while its general validity is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Richard W. Kenyon and David B. Wilson, “Spanning trees of graphs on surfaces and the intensity of loop-erased random walk on planar graphs”, arXiv:1107.3377 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3377

record.title: Fakhruddin's conjecture on the \mathfrak{sl}_2 conformal block cone of \overline{M}_{0,6}
record.statement: Let $\operatorname{Nef}(\overline{M}_{0,6})$ be the nef cone. A Fakhruddin ray is an extremal ray spanned either by $D(\mathfrak{sl}_2,1,(1,1,1,1,1,1))$ or by one of the 127 pullbacks from the GIT quotients $(\mathbb{P}^1)^n /\!/_{L} \operatorname{SL}_2$ studied in the source. A Fakhruddin orbit is an $S_6$-orbit of Fakhruddin rays, and the Fakhruddin cone is the subcone of $\operatorname{Nef}(\overline{M}_{0,6})$ spanned by Fakhruddin rays. **Fakhruddin's conjecture.** The cone generated by all $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ conformal block divisors for all levels is equal to the Fakhruddin cone. This conjecture identifies all such conformal block divisors with the specified extremal-ray cone in the nef cone of $\overline{M}_{0,6}$.
record.source_name: David Swinarski, “sl_2 conformal block divisors and the nef cone of M_0,n”, arXiv:1107.5331 (2011).

record.title: Realization conjecture for arithmetic invariants of hyperbolic 3-manifolds
record.statement: Let $k$ be a non-real concrete number field, and let $A$ be a quaternion algebra over $k$. For a hyperbolic manifold $M$, write $k$ and $A$ for its invariant trace field and invariant quaternion algebra, respectively. **Realization conjecture.** Every non-real concrete number field $k$ and every quaternion algebra over it arise as the invariant trace field and invariant quaternion algebra of some hyperbolic manifold. This question was first asked by Alan Reid and the author about 20 years earlier and is presented here as a conjecture; the proposed approach is explicitly described as tentative. The stronger assertion concerning arbitrary denominator-prime sets is stated separately only as an optimistic addition.
record.source_name: Walter D Neumann, “Realizing arithmetic invariants of hyperbolic 3-manifolds”, arXiv:1108.0062 (2011).

record.title: Hyperbolic torsion polynomial detection conjecture for hyperbolic knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot in $S^3$, with hyperbolic torsion polynomial $4\mathcal{T}_K4$. Let $x(K)$ denote the Thurston norm, equivalently the genus for a knot in $S^3$.

**Hyperbolic torsion polynomial detection conjecture.** The hyperbolic torsion polynomial $4\mathcal{T}_K4$ determines $x(K)$, or equivalently its genus. Moreover, $K$ is fibered if and only if $4\mathcal{T}_K4$ is monic.

This conjecture proposes that the canonical hyperbolic torsion polynomial detects both the Thurston norm and fibering, despite the generally limited reliability of Alexander-type polynomials. The computations described in the paper support it for all $313{,}209$ hyperbolic knots with at most 15 crossings, but no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Nathan M. Dunfield, Stefan Friedl and Nicholas Jackson, “Twisted Alexander polynomials of hyperbolic knots”, arXiv:1108.3045 (2012).

record.title: Order-preservation conjecture for equal-mass three-body syzygies
record.statement:
Let three equal masses be released from rest in a scalene triangular configuration whose side lengths satisfy

$$
r_{12}<r_{13}<r_{23}.
$$

Let $r_{ij}(t)$ be the distance between masses $i$ and $j$, and let $t$ be the instant of first syzygy. **Equal-mass order-preservation conjecture.** Under Newtonian attraction, the inequalities persist throughout the motion up to first syzygy:

$$
r_{12}(t)<r_{13}(t)<r_{23}(t).
$$

This is suggested by the preceding minimizer theorem, which establishes the corresponding inequalities for the relevant variational minimizers. The broader assertion for every equal-mass release from rest in such a scalene shape is presented as a conjecture, with no resolution supplied here.
record.source_name: Richard Moeckel, Richard Montgomery and Andrea Venturelli, “From Brake to Syzygy”, arXiv:1109.1089 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.1089

record.title: Conjecture on Wilf equivalence of 0021 and 1012
record.statement: For a pattern $p$, let $A_p(n)$ be the number of ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding $p$. Two patterns are **Wilf equivalent** if their avoidance sequences agree for every $n$. **The 0021–1012 Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** The patterns $0021$ and $1012$ are Wilf equivalent, and $A_{0021}(n)=A_{1012}(n)$ is given by the binomial transform of the Catalan numbers. The source gives no resolution of this proposed equivalence and enumeration.
record.source_name: Paul Duncan and Einar Steingrimsson, “Pattern avoidance in ascent sequences”, arXiv:1109.3641 (2011).

record.title: The universal critical-slope conjecture for copolymers near a selective interface
record.statement:
Let $h_c^\mathrm{que}(\beta)$ be the quenched critical curve and let

$$
K_c=\lim_{\beta\downarrow 0}\frac{h_c^\mathrm{que}(\beta)}{\beta},
$$

when this limit exists, for a copolymer model whose renewal exponent is $\alpha>1$. **Critical-slope conjecture.** The universal limit satisfies

$$
K_c=\frac{1+\alpha}{2\alpha}\quad\text{for all }\alpha>1.
$$

The value of $K_c$ is conjectured to be universal, depending only on the renewal exponent $\alpha$ and not on the fine details of the interaction Hamiltonian. Its existence is known for $1<\alpha<2$ under suitable assumptions, while for $\alpha\geq 2$ it remained open in the source; numerical work for simple random walk, corresponding to $\alpha=\tfrac32$, gives $K_c\in[0.82,0.84]$, consistent with the conjectured value $\tfrac56$.
record.source_name: E. Bolthausen, F. den Hollander and A. A. Opoku, “A copolymer near a selective interface: variational characterization of the free energy”, arXiv:1110.1315 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.1315

record.title: Conjecture on the three-dimensional vertex index
record.statement:
Let ${\bf K}$ be an arbitrary $0$-symmetric convex body in ${\mathbb R}^3$. A truncated octahedron of the form ${\bf T}-{\bf T}$ is obtained from an arbitrary tetrahedron ${\bf T}$ by Minkowski subtraction. **Three-dimensional vertex-index conjecture.**

$$
{\rm vein}({\bf K})\leq 12,
$$

with equality for truncated octahedra of the form ${\bf T}-{\bf T}$, where ${\bf T}$ is an arbitrary tetrahedron in ${\mathbb R}^3$. The source gives only a conjectural upper bound beyond its established estimate $18$, so the assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Karoly Bezdek and Alexander E. Litvak, “On the vertex index of convex bodies”, arXiv:1110.4334 (2011).

record.title: The conjecture on the validity of relation (6.24') for one-dimensional systems
record.statement:
Let $C$ and $
u$ be the parameters appearing in relation (6.24'), and let $L_s$ denote the function used there. For $n=1$ and $
u<0$, assume

$$
-C\nu\leq 1.
$$

Relation (6.24') is the inequality established in the preceding discussion for the corresponding Bose and Fermi cases. **Conjecture on relation (6.24').** Relation (6.24') should hold for all $-C\nu\leq 1$ when $n=1$ and $
u<0$. The text further verifies the extremal case $C\nu=-1$ by estimating $L_{3/2}(-1)/L_{1/2}(-1)>1$, but does not establish the full asserted range.

record.title: Conjecture on the number of Beauville p-groups of order p^5
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $g(p)$ denote the number of Beauville $p$-groups of order $p^{5}$, and let $H_3$ and $H_4$ be the groups referred to in the preceding construction. **The Beauville $p$-group counting conjecture.** For all $p\ge 5$,

$$
g(p)=p+10.
$$

In particular, $H_3$ and $H_4$ are Beauville groups for $p\ge 5$. The preceding work establishes the count for $5\leq p\leq 19$ and motivates the conjecture for all primes at least $5$.
record.source_name: Nathan Barker, Nigel Boston and Ben Fairbairn, “A Note on Beauville p-Groups”, arXiv:1111.3522 (2012).

record.title: Alon's divisibility conjecture for semicharacters of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. A **semicharacter** of $G$ is a function $f:G\rightarrow\mathbb{C}^{*}$ satisfying $f(ab)=f(a)f(b)$ whenever $a,b\in G$ commute. The semicharacters form an abelian group under pointwise multiplication, denoted by $\widehat{G}$. **Alon's divisibility conjecture.** The order of the group of semicharacters is divisible by the order of $G$:

$$
|G|\mid |\widehat{G}|.
$$

The conjecture extends the fact that for a finite abelian group, its character group has the same order as the group. The paper proves the divisibility for several important families, including symmetric groups and the groups $GL(2,q)$, and reports computational verification for all groups of order at most $255$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Gil Alon, “Semicharacters of Groups”, arXiv:1112.6125 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.6125

record.title: The sharp finite hexagonal-grid isoperimetric inequality
record.statement:
Let $G_r$ be the finite hexagonal grid graph of radius $r$, let $V(G_r)$ be its vertex set, and let $N(W)$ and ${\mathscr E}(W)$ denote the relevant vertex and edge neighborhoods of a finite subset $W\subseteq V(G_r)$. **Finite hexagonal-grid isoperimetric conjecture.** For every finite subset $W\subseteq V(G_r)$ with $|W|\leq 3r^2$, one has

$$
|N(W)|,|{\mathscr E}(W)|\geq \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{|W|}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the constants in the finite-grid isoperimetric theorem can be improved to the sharp-looking value $2/\sqrt{3}\approx 1.1547$; whether this improvement holds for all such subsets remains open in the source.

record.title: The p-integrality conjecture for the Narayana-related sequence
record.statement:
Let $\mu\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $a_n(\mu)$ be the sequence defined by the recurrence in the paper, with initial condition $a_1(\mu)$. A rational sequence is **$p$-integral** when every denominator is a power of the prime $p$.

**The p-integrality conjecture.** For every $\mu\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist an initial condition $a_1(\mu)$ and a prime $p$ such that the sequence $a_n(\mu)$ is $p$-integral.

The conjecture is motivated by computational examples, including $p=3,5,7,11$ and $13$ for $\mu=2,3,4,5,6,7$ and $8$, respectively. No proof or disproof is given in the source.

record.title: The c_2 residue conjecture for primitive log-divergent graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with graph polynomial $cPsi_G$, and let $I_G$ denote its Feynman residue when $G$ is primitive and overall logarithmically divergent. For graphs with at least three vertices, let $c_2(G)$ be the point-counting invariant defined by

$$
[X_G]_q \equiv c_2(G)_q q^2 \pmod{q^3},
$$

where $X_G\subset \mathbb{A}^{N_G}$ is the affine graph hypersurface defined by $cPsi_G=0$.

**The $c_2$ residue conjecture.** If $I_{G_1}=I_{G_2}$ for two primitive log-divergent graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, then

$$
c_2(G_1)=c_2(G_2).
$$

This conjecture says that the $c_2$ invariant depends only on the Feynman residue whenever it is defined. It was verified for all graphs with at most $14$ edges, but its general status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Francis Brown, Oliver Schnetz and Karen Yeats, “Properties of c_2 invariants of Feynman graphs”, arXiv:1203.0188 (2012).

record.title: Coefficient-positivity conjecture for the multivariate type $D$ Eulerian polynomial
record.statement:
For $n\geq 2$, let $D_n(\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y})$ be the multivariate refinement defined by

$$
D_n(\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y})=B_n(\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y};1)-n2^{n-1}x_ny_nA_{n-2}(\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y}).
$$

Here $A_{n-2}$ and $B_n$ are the stable multivariate refinements of the type $A$ and type $B$ Eulerian polynomials, respectively. **Coefficient-positivity conjecture.**

$$
D_n(\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y})\in\mathbb{N}[\mathbold{x},\mathbold{y}]
$$

for all $n\geq 2$. The conjecture was verified by computer for $n\leq 11$; if true, it could yield a refinement of the type $D$ descent statistic and a new recursion for type $D$ Eulerian polynomials.
record.source_name: Mirkó Visontai and Nathan Williams, “Stable multivariate W-Eulerian polynomials”, arXiv:1203.0791 (2013).

record.title: The tau-conjecture on integer roots of straight-line polynomials
record.statement:
For $f\in\mathbb{Z}[T]$, define $\tau(f)$ as the least $k$ for which $f$ occurs in a sequence beginning with $f_{-1}(T)=1$ and $f_0(T)=T$, with each later polynomial obtained from two earlier ones by addition, subtraction, or multiplication. Let $Z(f)$ be the number of distinct integer zeros of $f$. **The $\tau$-conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
Z(f)\leq(1+\tau(f))^c
$$

for every $f\in\mathbb{Z}[T]$. This conjecture would imply that the 20 Questions problem is not in polynomial time; its status is open in the source.
record.source_name: Joshua A. Grochow and Korben Rusek, “Report on "Mathematical Aspects of P vs. NP and its Variants."”, arXiv:1203.2888 (2012).

record.title: The umbral moonshine multiplier-system conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Lambda=\{2,3,4,5,7,13\}$, let $G^{(\ell)}$ be the corresponding umbral group, and let $H^{(\ell)}_g$ be its vector-valued mock modular McKay–Thompson series. For each $g\in G^{(\ell)}$, let $(n_g,h_g)$ be the associated pair and let $\nu^{(\ell)}_{n|h}$ be the corresponding multiplier system on $\Gamma_0(n)$. **Umbral moonshine multiplier-system conjecture.** For all $\ell\in\Lambda$ and $g\in G^{(\ell)}$, the multiplier system of $H^{(\ell)}_g$ is $\nu^{(\ell)}_{n|h}$ with $n=n_g$ and $h=h_g$. The conjecture gives the predicted multipliers for all umbral McKay–Thompson series; the source does not establish it independently.

record.title: The umbral module doublet conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda=\{2,3,4,5,7,13\}$ and let $K^{(\ell)}_{r,-D/4\ell}$ be the corresponding representation of $G^{(\ell)}$. Say that a $G$-module is a **doublet** if it is isomorphic to the direct sum of two copies of a single representation. **Umbral module doublet conjecture.** The representation $K^{(\ell)}_{r,-D/4\ell}$ is a doublet if and only if

$$
D\neq -n\lambda^2
$$

for every integer $\lambda$ and every $n$ satisfying the conditions of the cited proposition. This conjecture predicts precisely when the conjectural graded pieces are doublets; it remains open in the source.

record.title: Dokos–Dwyer–Johnson–Sagan–Selsor coefficient-parity conjecture for 321-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
For each integer $k\geq 0$, let $M_{2^k-1}(321;q)$ denote the major-index generating polynomial associated with 321-avoiding permutations of length $2^k-1$, and write $\langle q^i\rangle$ for the coefficient of $q^i$. **Dokos–Dwyer–Johnson–Sagan–Selsor's coefficient-parity conjecture.** For all $k\geq 0$,

$$
\langle q^i\rangle M_{2^k-1}(321;q)=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } i=0,\\
\text{an even number} & \text{if } i\geq 1.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture concerns the parity of the coefficients in the major-index generating polynomial for 321-avoiding permutations at lengths one less than powers of two. The source attributes it to Dokos, Dwyer, Johnson, Sagan and Selsor as their Conjecture 3.6; no resolution is given here.

record.title: The cuspidal cohomology conjecture for prime ideals in imaginary quadratic fields
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field, let ${\mathcal O}_K$ be its ring of integers, and let $\Gamma_0({\mathfrak p})$ denote the corresponding congruence subgroup for a prime ideal ${\mathfrak p}$ of residue degree one. **Cuspidal cohomology conjecture.** For every $K$, there are infinitely many such prime ideals ${\mathfrak p}$ for which

$$
H^1_{cusp}(\Gamma_0({\mathfrak p}),\mathbb C) \not= 0.
$$

The conjecture concerns the apparent uniform distribution of the prime ideals for which cuspidal cohomology does not vanish; the surrounding data suggest that vanishing occurs for roughly $90\%$ of the relevant primes. It is also related to the existence of abelian varieties over imaginary quadratic fields with special endomorphism rings and restricted ramification.

record.title: Existence of bounded-volume, arbitrarily large-link-volume 3-manifolds
record.statement:
Let $v_{3}$ denote the volume of a regular ideal tetrahedron. Consider closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds, with hyperbolic volume $\vol[M]$ and link volume $\lv[M]$.

**Bounded-volume, arbitrarily large-link-volume conjecture.** For every $V>0$ there exists a manifold $M$ so that

$$
\vol[M] < 2v_{3} = 2.029\dots
$$

and

$$
\lv[M] > V.
$$

This is presented as an implication of the preceding slope conjecture, using Dehn fillings of the figure-eight knot exterior. It formalizes the claim that link volume can be arbitrarily large among manifolds whose hyperbolic volume remains below the volume of the figure-eight knot complement; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Yo'av Rieck and Yasushi Yamashita, “The Link Volume of 3-Manifolds”, arXiv:1205.1274 (2012).

record.title: Goldman's volume rigidity conjecture for uniform lattices
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a uniform lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group $G$ with trivial center and no compact factors. Let $X$ be the associated symmetric space, let $M=\Gamma\backslash X$, and let $\rho\colon \Gamma\to G$ be a representation. Its volume invariant satisfies

$$
|\upsilon(\rho)|\leq \operatorname{Vol}(M).
$$

**Goldman's volume rigidity conjecture.** Equality holds if and only if $\rho$ is a discrete, faithful representation of $\Gamma$ into $G$.
Goldman proved this conjecture for all connected semisimple Lie groups except $\mathrm{SU}(n,1)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(n,1)$, and $\mathrm{F}_4^{-20}$; the source presents the equality characterization as conjectural in the remaining cases.
record.source_name: Sungwoon Kim and Inkang Kim, “Volume invariant and maximal representations of discrete subgroups of Lie groups”, arXiv:1205.4787 (2012).

record.title: The exact integer complexity conjecture for powers of 2 and 3
record.statement:
Let $\|n\|$ denote the least number of ones needed to write the positive integer $n$ using addition, multiplication, and parentheses. For integers $a,k\geq 0$ with $a+k\geq 1$, consider the integer $2^a\cdot 3^k$. **Exact integer complexity conjecture.** For all $a\geq 0$ and all $k\geq 0$ with $a+k\geq 1$, one has

$$
\|2^a\cdot 3^k\|=2a+3k.
$$

This asserts that the standard factorization gives an optimal expression for every positive integer composed only of the primes $2$ and $3$. The statement was supported by the exact results for several ranges of $a$ and by computational verification up to $10^{12}$, but its general status is open.
record.source_name: Harry Altman and Joshua Zelinsky, “Numbers with Integer Complexity Close to the Lower Bound”, arXiv:1207.4841 (2012).

record.title: Conjecture on arbitrarily long zero gaps in the privileged complexity of the Thue–Morse word
record.statement: Let $t$ be the Thue–Morse word, and let $\mathpzc{A}_n(t)$ denote the number of privileged factors of $t$ of length $n$. A **zero gap** is a consecutive interval of lengths on which $\mathpzc{A}_n(t)=0$. **Zero-gap conjecture.** There exist arbitrarily long, but not infinite, zero gaps in the values of $\mathpzc{A}_n(t)$. The conjecture is based on computer searches and observed gaps of zeros, including a gap for every $n$ with $189\leq n\leq257$; the existence of arbitrarily long finite gaps remains open.

record.title: Stability of the regular n-gon at the bifurcation point
record.statement: Let $n$ be the number of vortices and consider the regular $n$-gon at the bifurcation point, with stability determined by the positivity of the relevant quadratic form. **Stability conjecture.** For all values of $n$, the $n$-gon is stable at the bifurcation point. The paper establishes stability numerically for several cases, including $n=5$, $n=7$, $n=9$, and $n=11$, but does not provide a proof for all values of $n$.

record.title: Nakamura's extremal conjecture for non-overlapping patterns
record.statement:
Let $ath]σ\in\mathcal S_m$ be a **non-overlapping pattern**, and let $\alpha_n(σ)$ be the number of permutations of length $n$ avoiding $ath]σ$. **Nakamura's extremal conjecture.** For every non-overlapping $ath]σ\in\mathcal S_m$, there exists $n_0$ such that, for all $n\geq n_0$,

$$
\alpha_n(123\dots(m-2)m(m-1))\leq\alpha_n(σ)\leq\alpha_n(134\dots m2).
$$

The lower and upper bounds assert respectively that $123\dots(m-2)m(m-1)$ is hardest to avoid and $134\dots m2$ is easiest to avoid among non-overlapping patterns of length $m$. The source presents this as an open conjecture motivated by numerical evidence.
record.source_name: Sergi Elizalde and Marc Noy, “Clusters, generating functions and asymptotics for consecutive patterns in permutations”, arXiv:1210.6061 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.6061

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2012). “The following conjecture, which is equivalent to the fact that the monotone pattern has the largest growth constant among patterns of the same length, is still open.”

record.title: The Haiman–Loehr conjecture for higher $q,t$-Catalan polynomials
record.statement:
Let $C^{(m)}_n(q,t)$ denote the combinatorial higher $q,t$-Catalan polynomial, and let $AC^{(m)}_n(q,t)$ be the Garsia–Haiman expression

$$
AC^{(m)}_n(q,t)=\sum_{\mu\in\operatorname{Par}(n)}\frac{T_{\mu}^{m+1}(1-q)(1-t)B_{\mu}\Pi_{\mu}}{w_{\mu}},
$$

where the sum is over partitions of $n$ and $T_{\mu}$, $B_{\mu}$, $\Pi_{\mu}$, and $w_{\mu}$ are defined from the arm, coarm, leg, and coleg statistics of the cells of the partition diagram. **Haiman–Loehr conjecture.** For all $m,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$,

$$
C^{(m)}_n(q,t)=AC^{(m)}_n(q,t).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the combinatorial and Garsia–Haiman formulas agree. It has been open since approximately 2001; the case $m=1$ follows from the theorem of Garsia, Haglund, and Haiman.
record.source_name: Kyungyong Lee, Li Li and Nicholas A. Loehr, “Combinatorics of certain higher q,t-Catalan polynomials: chains, joint symmetry, and the Garsia-Haiman formula”, arXiv:1211.2191 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.2191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

record.title: Prime-dimension existence conjecture for binary Steiner structures
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a prime satisfying

$$
n \equiv 1 \pmod{6},\qquad n\geq 13.
$$

A **coset complete 3-dimensional subspace** is a 3-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ used as a generator for the construction described in the paper. **Prime-dimension existence conjecture.** There exists a Steiner structure $\mathbb{S}_2[2,3,n]$ generated by a set of $\frac{2^n-2}{42n}$ pairwise disjoint coset complete 3-dimensional subspaces. The constructed example $\mathbb{S}_2[2,3,13]$ provides supporting evidence, but the asserted existence for all indicated primes remains open.
record.source_name: Tuvi Etzion and Alexander Vardy, “q-Analogs of Steiner Systems”, arXiv:1211.2393 (2012).

record.title: Faber–Zagier relations conjecture for the tautological ring of the moduli space of curves
record.statement:
Let $R^*({\mathcal{M}}_g)$ be the tautological ring of the moduli space of smooth genus-$g$ curves, let $\kappa_i$ denote its kappa classes, and let

$$
q:\mathbb{Q}[\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3,\ldots]\longrightarrow R^*({\mathcal{M}}_g)\longrightarrow 0
$$

be the natural quotient map. Denote by $\mathsf{FZ}_g$ the ideal generated by the Faber–Zagier relations.

**Faber–Zagier relations conjecture.** For all $g\geq 2$, the kernel of $q$ is the Faber–Zagier ideal $\mathsf{FZ}_g$.

The conjecture asserts that the Faber–Zagier relations generate all relations among the kappa classes. It is consistent with the computations described in the source, but remains open; in genus $24$ the Faber–Zagier relations do not give the predicted Gorenstein quotient.
record.source_name: R. Pandharipande and A. Pixton, “Relations in the tautological ring of the moduli space of curves”, arXiv:1301.4561 (2020).

record.title: Large-cardinal dichotomy for abstract elementary classes
record.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak k}$ be an abstract elementary class. **Large-cardinal dichotomy conjecture.** For a closed unbounded class $C$ of cardinals, the alternatives stated in the source should hold: (1) the promised conclusion of Theorem 28 can be obtained with $C$ an end segment of $\{\mu:\mu=\beth_{1,\mu}\}$, or with $C=\{\mu:\mu=\beth_{2,\mu}\}$; and (2) for every such ${\mathfrak k}$, either

$$
M\in K^{\mathfrak k}_\lambda\wedge\lambda\in C\wedge {\rm cf}(\lambda)=\aleph_0\Rightarrow \Upsilon^{\rm or}_\lambda[\mathfrak k_M]\neq\emptyset,
$$

or

$$
\lambda\in C\wedge {\rm cf}(\lambda)=\aleph_0\Rightarrow \dot I(\lambda,K_{\mathfrak k})\geq 2^\lambda\text{ (or at least }\lambda^+\text{)}.
$$

The source says that part (1) is intended for a continuation; the claims are therefore unresolved.
record.source_name: Saharon Shelah, “A.E.C. with not too many models”, arXiv:1302.4841 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4841

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: The linear connectivity conjecture for linked tournaments
record.statement:
A **tournament** is an orientation of a complete graph. A tournament is **strongly $r$-connected** when deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves a strongly connected digraph. A tournament is **$k$-linked** if, for every choice of $k$ distinct initial vertices and $k$ distinct terminal vertices, there are $k$ vertex-disjoint directed paths linking the prescribed pairs.

**Linear connectivity conjecture for linked tournaments.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every strongly $Ck$-connected tournament is $k$-linked.

The paper proves a near-linear bound, namely strong $10^4k\log k$-connectivity implies $k$-linkedness, and notes that removing the logarithmic factor remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn, John Lapinskas, Deryk Osthus and Viresh Patel, “Proof of a conjecture of Thomassen on Hamilton cycles in highly connected tournaments”, arXiv:1303.4213 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4213

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: Atkin's 13-adic congruences for normalized coefficients of the j-function
record.statement:
Let $j(z)=q^{-1}+744+196884q+\cdots$, write $j=\sum_n c_n(j)q^n$, and for a positive integer $m$ with $c_{p^m}(j)\neq0$ define

$$
t_m(j,n)=\frac{c_{np^m}(j)}{c_{p^m}(j)}.
$$

**Atkin's conjecture.** For any prime $p\neq13$ such that $c_{p^m}(j)\neq0$ for all $m\geq1$,

$$
t_m(j,np)-t_m(j,n)t_m(j,p)+p^{-1}t_m(j,n/p)\equiv0\pmod{13^m},\qquad \forall m,n\geq1,
$$

and

$$
t_m(j,13n)-t_m(j,n)t_m(j,13)\equiv0\pmod{13^m},\qquad \forall m,n\geq1.
$$

The source states that this conjecture was proved by Koike and Katz using the convergence of repeated applications of $U_{13}$ to a single $13$-adic Hecke eigenform. Related conjectures for primes $p\leq23$ were also established, so this claim is solved.
record.source_name: Wen-Ching Winnie Li and Ling Long, “Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer congruences and noncongruence modular forms”, arXiv:1303.6228 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.6228

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2013). “This conjecture was proved in .”

record.title: Positivity rigidity conjecture for a binomial finite-difference sum
record.statement:
Fix $s\in\mathbb{N}^+$, $q\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, $\widetilde{q}\in\mathbb{R}$ with $\widetilde{q}>0$, and real numbers $p_m$ for $m=0,1,\ldots,s+1$. Suppose that, for every $k=0,1,\ldots,s+1$,

$$
\sum_{m=0}^{\min(k,s)}\binom{s-1+k-m}{s-1}p_mq^m(-\widetilde{q})^{k-m}\geq 0.
$$

**Positivity rigidity conjecture.** Then $p_0\geq 0$, and for $m=1,2,\ldots,s+1$,

$$
p_m=p_0\binom{s}{m}\left(\frac{\widetilde{q}}{q}\right)^m.
$$

Moreover, the sum equals $p_0$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k=1,2,\ldots,s+1$. The conjecture was verified by Mathematica for $1\leq s\leq 10$ and proved manually for $s=2$, but its general status is unresolved.
record.source_name: Lajos Loczi and David I. Ketcheson, “Rational functions with maximal radius of absolute monotonicity”, arXiv:1303.6651 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.6651

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2013). “Conjectures , , and were previously proved only in the cases $s=1$ or $s=2$.”

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for forbidden graphs of bounded algebraic co-rank
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma_{\leq k}$ denote the class of simple graphs with algebraic co-rank at most $k$, and let ${\bf Forb}(\Gamma_{\leq k})$ be the set of graphs that do not contain a graph in $\Gamma_{\leq k}$ as an induced subgraph. **Finiteness conjecture.** For all $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the set

$$
{\bf Forb}(\Gamma_{\leq k})
$$

is finite. The paper establishes that this set is nonempty for every $k\geq 0$ and notes that the case $k=3$ has been shown to contain $49$ graphs; finiteness for all $k$ remains conjectural.
